title: Samsung Galaxy Watch 9 vs Apple Watch Series 11: The wearables compared
summary: A head-to-head look at the Samsung Galaxy Watch 9 and Apple Watch Series 11 highlights key differences: OS and phone compatibility (One UI/WearOS for Android vs watchOS for iPhone), chipset (Snapdragon Wear Elite with an NPU and Gemini support vs Apple S10), pricing and sizes, and broadly similar health and fitness tracking. Choice will mostly depend on your smartphone ecosystem, with extra considerations for preferred size and whether you want Ultra rugged variants.

Looking for an easy way to track your health and workouts, but are torn between a Samsung or Apple offering? You’ve come to the right place.

Sure, while the decision between theSamsung Galaxy Watch 9and the Apple Watch Series 11 will mostly boil down to whether you’re sporting a Samsung or an iPhone, there are a few other differences that are worth keeping in mind.

While we’re yet to conclusively review either smartwatch, we’ve compared the specs of the Galaxy Watch 9 to the Apple Watch Series 11 and highlighted the main differences between the two below.

Once you’re finished here, check out ourSamsung Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 vs Apple Watch Ultra 3comparison, while ourSamsung Galaxy Watch 9 vs Watch 8guide explains what’s new with this year’s flagship wearable. Finally, our round ups of thebest smartwatchesandbest fitness trackerswill help you find your next device.

The Samsung Galaxy Watch 9 has a starting price of £349 and is currently available for pre-order ahead of its official launch on August 7th.

On the other hand, the Apple Watch Series 11 is available to buy now with an RRP of £369 for the aluminium iteration. This price rises quite substantially up to £649 for the titanium option.

One of the biggest differences between the Galaxy Watch 9 and the Apple Watch Series 11 is with their respective operating systems. While the Galaxy Watch 9 runs on Samsung’s custom One UI that’s based on Google’s WearOS, the Apple Watch 11 uses Apple’s own WatchOS platform.

This means that while the Samsung Galaxy Watch 9 can be paired with mostAndroid phones(although for the best experience, you’re better off pairing it with a Samsung handset), whereas the Apple Watch 11 can only be paired with an iPhone. As we mentioned earlier, this alone will likely bethedeciding factor when choosing between the smartwatches.

For a closer look at the differences, visit our dedicatedWatchOS vs WearOSguide.

Powering the Galaxy Watch 9 is Qualcomm’s latest wearable chip, Snapdragon Wear Elite. Not only does Snapdragon Wear Elite promise to boost performance by up to 35%, but it’s also the world’s first wearable platform that features a dedicated NPU for personal AI. That means the Galaxy Watch 9 can now support hands-free access to Gemini too.

In comparison, the Apple Watch 11 is powered by Apple’s S10 chip which is the same that powers the Apple Watch Series 10 and Apple Watch SE 3 too. While we’re yet to specifically review the Watch 11, we have spent time with theApple Watch Series 10and found it to be a solid performer and able to do everything from measure data and record activity to open Siri without any delay. With this in mind, we’d reasonably expect the Apple Watch 11 to provide a similar performance.

When it comes to health and fitness tracking, generally the Galaxy Watch 9 and Apple Watch 11 are evenly matched. Both are equipped with heart rate, blood pressure and other Vitals monitoring, GPS for accurate location pinning and great sleep tracking tools too, including sleep apnea notifications too. In fact, our Mobile Editor Lewis Painter was notified of his potentialsleep apnea with last year’s Galaxy Watch 8.

However, the Apple Watch Series 11 also benefits from hypertension notifications which should alert users for signs of chronic high blood pressure.

Both the Galaxy Watch 9 and the Apple Watch Series 11 are hailed as being everyday smartwatches that are just the right side of sporty. If you prefer the more rugged, adventurous design then you’d be better off opting for the Ultra alternatives for both the Galaxy Watch and Apple Watch.

While both come in a choice between two sizes, the Apple Watch Series 11’s options are larger than the Galaxy Watch 9. So, while the Galaxy Watch 9 comes as either a 40mm or 44mm size, the Apple Watch 11 is available as a 42mm or 46mm.

Whether you prefer the larger Apple Watch 11 or the smallest Galaxy Watch 9 will depend on your personal preference. For example, our Editor Max Parker loved the 46mm Apple Watch 10, and found it comfortable and easy to use.

Deciding between the Samsung Galaxy Watch 9 and the Apple Watch Series 11 will mainly boil down to what smartphone you have. If you’re sporting an Android, or better yet a Samsung Galaxy, then the Galaxy Watch 9 is the one for you. On the other hand if you’re a devout iPhone user, then the Apple Watch Series 11 is your best option.

Jess joined the Trusted Reviews team early in 2024, after working for almost three years in lifestyle and technology PR. Using the skills gained from her previous role, Jess has taken on a new challenge, taking the plunge into writing and journalism, with a particular interest in smart home technology. She is also an English graduate from Goldsmiths College and when she’s not typing away at her desk, Jess loves to travel, with her favourite places being Rio de Janeiro, Barcelona and Rome.
